## CEO overview

What is changing: Firstmate now stops repeatedly asking about paused work that has already finished or been frozen after its worker has gone away.
  It still asks again when a worker is present, an outside dependency is genuinely pending, another mate is waiting, or the work may actually be stuck.
Why it matters: The previous behavior could wake Firstmate every hour forever because the last message still said paused even though nobody remained to answer the recheck.
Customer or business impact: The captain receives fewer meaningless supervision alerts during normal work and walk-away periods, while real waits, held decisions, and stuck work remain visible.
Risk and rollout: Risk is low because silence applies only to ordinary work that is both proven complete or captain-frozen and proven to have no live worker.
  That conclusion expires and is checked again, and any failed, resumed, live, uncertain, or secondmate work continues through the existing alert path.
  The captain retains merge authority, and the outer executor must synchronize this narrative into the live pull request while preserving its machine-owned `## Pipeline` section before requiring every hosted check on the final head.

## What changed technically

- Added one shared declared-wait classification that combines authoritative crew state, worker kind, and backend agent liveness for normal and away-mode supervision.
- Settled stale `paused:` and verified `captain-held` declarations only for dead ordinary workers on completed or parked lanes, with an expiring classification that revalidates state and liveness.
- Routed unchanged and changing pane hashes through the same marker-aware watcher handling so live and uncertain waits surface once, genuine waits keep their bounded cadence, resumed work keeps wedge aging, and invalidated settlements surface immediately.
- Kept every secondmate declaration on its bounded recheck cadence without reading remote secondmate state or endpoint liveness, preventing remote transport from blocking away-mode housekeeping.
- Limited away-mode reclassification to the stale due boundary once stale tracking owns a lane, preserving bounded housekeeping and wedge detection for working or failed lanes whose status log still ends in `paused:`.
- Added executable watcher and daemon regressions for changing-hash re-arms, settlement expiry, live and uncertain waits, secondmate holds, resumed and failed work, and persistent wedges.
- Updated the supervision architecture, configuration reference, Herdr integration note, and away-mode skill to describe settlement eligibility and the preserved recheck paths.

## Module-boundary decision

Module-boundary decision: Current modules retained.
  The shared state-and-liveness decision belongs in `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`, normal watcher marker transitions belong in `bin/fm-watch.sh`, and away-mode tracking belongs in `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh`.
  This keeps one classification contract without creating another supervisor or duplicating backend policy.
